rationale: The printed entry's core is carried directly by the four cited texts read together: Deut 30:19-20 and Lev 18:5 explicitly equate 'life' with covenant obedience ('choose life… he is thy life'; 'if a man do, he shall live in them'), Matt 7:14 makes the narrow way the path that 'leadeth unto life,' and John 14:6 identifies Jesus as that same triad. The chapter supplies the linking mechanics (derek as conduct, law as truth/standard, life as the resulting covenant existence) without adding material claims to the glossary sentence itself. The strongest counter (Johannine zōē as eternal/divine life or Christ-title) explains the John verse in isolation but leaves the two Torah texts and the Matt 7:14 collocation under-explained or reassigned to a different sense of 'life.' No supplied detail is left unaccounted for by the entry, and none is better explained by the counter.
book_core_identification: Covenant existence—the life lived walking in the Way according to God's law.
chapter_only_objections: Extended equation of 'the life' with 'the light' via John 1:4 and the still-unpublished Light chapter
Tree-of-life = covenant people / law complex drawn from Prov 3:18
Highway (mesillah) vs. way (derek) distinction and Isaiah 35/40 highway imagery
Door/posts = law + Passover blood typology for Christ as door
Flaming sword of Gen 3:24 = word of God guarding the way
strongest_counter_interpretation: In the decisive NT occurrences (esp. with the article), 'the life' is the eternal/divine zōē that is identical with or given by the person of Jesus Christ—qualitatively different from biological or merely covenantal existence—and is received by faith/union rather than defined as Torah-shaped conduct.
counter_core_identification: Eternal/divine life (zōē) embodied in and mediated by Jesus Christ himself.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that the primary referent of 'the life' is the covenant existence produced by walking according to God's law; it relocates the referent to Christological/eternal life independent of that Torah definition.
counter_case: John 14:6 and 11:25 function as absolute 'I am' titles paralleling other christological absolutes, not as restatements of Deuteronomic covenant life
John 1:4; 5:26; 1 John 1:1-2; 5:11-12 repeatedly locate 'the life' in the Son as its source and content, received by believing rather than by doing the statutes
The Johannine present-possession formulas ('has passed from death to life,' 'has eternal life') emphasize relational knowledge of God (John 17:3) over Torah conduct as the definition of life itself
Standard lexical distinction zōē vs. bios/psychē is widely attested and favors qualitative divine life over covenant existence
book_explanatory_advantages: Single coherent sense spans the two Torah texts, Matt 7:14 and John 14:6 without sense-shifting
Explains why 'the way… leadeth unto life' (Matt 7:14) and why Jesus can claim to be both the way and the life in one breath
Accounts for the definite article by pointing to the already-defined covenant life of Deut/Lev rather than an undefined new entity
Preserves the OT witness pattern required by the book's own method and by the Berean test cited in the introduction
counter_explanatory_advantages: Fits the broader Johannine cluster (John 1, 5, 6, 10, 11, 17; 1 John) more immediately
Aligns with the dominant historic Christian reading of the title 'the Life'
decisive_sources: Chapter derivation linking derek/way → law/truth → covenant life
